chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man fell ill and so left the nafilah prayer.
He said: O Muhammad, it is not obligatory. If he makes it up, then it is a good deed that he does, and if he does not do it, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no obligation or liability upon him
key_terms.قَضَاهَا: made it up after missing it

ai.seo_question: Is a sick person required to make up missed nafilah prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the nafilah prayer is not obligatory, so a person who misses it due to illness is not liable for leaving it. If he later makes it up, that is a meritorious act, but if he does not, no duty remains upon him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1431 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrates that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"I asked him about a man who became ill and thus did not perform the supererogatory (nafilah) prayers.
Imam (as) said: 'O’ Muhammad, they are not obligatory. If he makes them up, it is a good deed he performs, and if he does not, there is no obligation upon him.'"
